knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 2.5.1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly states the central limit theorem for an IID sequence and what it approximates?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the CLT statement and its target object.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: CLT targets the sample mean (or its standardised form) under IID with finite variance. Casual Normal habit, single-X claims, or requiring a Normal population misstate the theorem.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: IID, finite mean/variance → sample mean ≈ Normal for large n.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Normal-by-habit, CLT on one observation, or population must be Normal.

choices.label: For an IID sequence with finite mean and variance, the distribution of the sample mean X̄ (equivalently a standardised X̄) approaches Normal as n grows, giving a Normal approximation for sample-mean probabilities under stated conditions.
The CLT says every insurance quantity is Normal, so any routine Normal model needs no theorem statement or IID conditions.
The CLT approximates the distribution of a single observation X₁ as Normal whenever the population has a finite mean, regardless of sample size.
The CLT applies only when the population is already Normal; for non-Normal populations the sample mean cannot be approximated.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: CLT probability for sample mean
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Repair costs are iid with mean μ = 1200 and standard deviation σ = 300. A sample of n = 36 repairs is drawn. Using the CLT and Φ(1) ≈ 0.841, approximate P(X̄ < 1150). Enter the probability as a decimal.
knowledge_checks.body: Standardise the sample mean under the CLT and evaluate the lower tail.
hints: First form sd(X̄) = σ/√n, then z = (1150 - 1200)/sd(X̄).
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using σ = 300 instead of σ/√n = 50 so that z = -1/6, or reporting Φ(1) ≈ 0.841 as the lower-tail probability itself.
success_criteria: Uses σ/√n when standardising, and converts Φ(1) to the lower tail.

worked_example.title: CLT probability for a mean repair cost
worked_example.problem_statement: Repair costs are iid with mean μ = 1200 and standard deviation σ = 300. A sample of n = 36 repairs is drawn. Using the CLT, approximate P(X̄ < 1150). Use Φ(1) ≈ 0.841.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Form the sampling sd σ/√n first, then standardise 1150 before reading Φ.

steps.label: Standard error of the sample mean
steps.explanation: Under the CLT for iid observations, X̄ is approximately Normal with mean μ and sd σ/√n.

steps.label: Standardise and evaluate the lower tail
steps.attempt_cue: Form z = (1150 − 1200)/50, then convert with Φ.
steps.explanation: The probability is the lower Normal tail at z = −1, equal to 1 − Φ(1).

steps.label: Refuse σ in place of σ/√n
steps.attempt_cue: State why using sd = 300 for X̄ is wrong.
steps.explanation: The CLT approximates the distribution of the sample mean, whose spread shrinks by √n. Using the population sd as if it were sd(X̄) ignores that reduction.

worked_example.final_answer: X̄ ≈ Normal(1200, 50); z = −1; P(X̄ < 1150) ≈ 0.159. Casual Normal use without stating the IID CLT sampling sd is not the same skill.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using X̄ ≈ Normal(1200, 300) and computing z = (1150 − 1200)/300 = −1/6, or reading Φ(1) ≈ 0.841 as the lower-tail probability itself.
